newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea plans to liberalise phone service charges.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea plans to liberalise phone service charges.

text.p: South Korea's Information and Communication Ministry said on Friday it would allow phone service providers to set their own prices in line with the opening of the domestic telecommunications market next year.

A ministry statement said the government had drafted legislation to change current telecommunication rules to comply with concessions to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and to encourage competition.
The ministry would submit the draft to parliament in June, after consultations with related ministries.
At present, the cabinet, with presidential approval, has control of phone service charges for local and long-distance calls.
The local telephone service is currently monopolised by state-run Korea Telecom. But the government would license a second local phone service provider in 1999.

The statement reaffirmed a move by the finance and economy ministry to allow 20 percent foreign ownership in Korea Telecom from 1998 and 33 percent from 2001. This would enable foreigners to hold Korea Telecom shares by acquiring depositary receipts issued by the telephone giant.

The statement said the government also would ease restrictions in some services including Internet telephony, leased line resale and local area networks, which it classified as "special service providers".
The government would simplify entry into the business by allowing registration after companies meet certain criteria.
To upgrade local area networks, the government would allow a new type of telecom operator, specialising in operating building communications operations.
The new law was expected to come into effect three months after paliamentary approval.
